To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the speciation analysis of trace levels of chromium in environmental matrices is possible using the on-line methods based on solid-phase and/or liquid-liquid extraction, which are coupled with various detection methods.
the most promising analytical strategies are based on the use of novel sorbents and on-line miniaturization of flow systems.
the use of novel materials for the selective separation/preconcentration and determination of chromium species is a very promising strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new on-line methods for chromium speciation in environmental samples.
the development of new methods for the speciation analysis of metals and metalloids.
the development of new analytical procedures based on on-line sample pretreatment and speciation of chromium in environmental matrices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the on-line flow systems are a very useful tool for speciation analysis of metals in environmental samples.
the use of on-line methods based on extraction for chromium speciation is an attractive alternative to the traditional off-line methods, and the use of these methods is still growing.

the on-line speciation of Cr(III)/Cr(VI) in various environmental matrices is still a great challenge for analytical chemists, but the recent advances in on-line methods based on extraction for speciation analysis of this element are promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of new materials and miniaturized flow systems has led to a new generation of on-line speciation methods.
the on-line speciation of chromium is a powerful tool for the analysis of environmental samples and that it has a promising future.

on-line methods based on extraction are very promising in chromium speciation, and they have been successfully applied for the determination of Cr(III)/Cr(VI) in various samples, e.g. environmental water, biological samples, and food.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of new materials for solid-phase extraction and new approaches to sample preparation, separation, and detection are important for further progress in speciation analysis of metals in environmental samples.
the use of on-line systems in chromium speciation is a powerful tool that enables automation of sample treatment, preconcentration, separation, and determination.
flow-based systems have become indispensable tools in the analysis of chromium speciation in environmental samples.
